trigger: Find a pair in a SORTED array that sums to a target
notes: Move left up if sum is too small, right down if too big. O(n). If the array is unsorted, use the hashmap-complement pattern instead.

trigger: Find a pair that sums to a target in an UNSORTED array
pattern: One pass with a hashmap of seen values (look up target - x)
notes: O(n) time, O(n) space. Beats sorting (O(n log n)) when indexes must be preserved.

trigger: Longest/shortest CONTIGUOUS subarray or substring satisfying a constraint
pattern: Sliding window: grow the right edge, shrink the left while the constraint is violated
notes: O(n) because each index enters and leaves the window once. Fixed-size variants: maintain a running sum/count.

trigger: Many range-sum queries, or count subarrays with sum exactly k
pattern: Prefix sums; for count-with-sum-k, a hashmap of prefix-sum frequencies
notes: sum(i..j) = prefix[j+1] - prefix[i]. The hashmap trick turns O(n^2) into O(n).

trigger: Overlapping intervals: merge them, count rooms, or insert one
pattern: Sort by start, then a single sweep comparing against the last kept interval
notes: O(n log n) from the sort. Overlap test after sorting: current.start <= last.end.

trigger: k largest / k smallest / k most frequent elements
pattern: Keep a heap of size k
notes: O(n log k), better than full sort when k << n. Python: heapq.nlargest / a min-heap of size k. Java: PriorityQueue.

trigger: Next greater element, daily temperatures, largest rectangle in histogram
pattern: Monotonic stack: push indexes, pop while the invariant would break
notes: Each index is pushed and popped at most once, so O(n) despite the nested loop.

trigger: Anagram checks, grouping by letters, character-count comparisons
pattern: Canonical key in a hashmap: sorted string (safe default) or 26-slot count array (lowercase-only optimization)
notes: The 26-array is O(m) vs O(m log m), but ord(c)-ord('a') throws on ANY non-lowercase char - a hidden test with 'A' or ' ' crashes it. Under assessment conditions, the sorted-string key wins unless the constraint guarantees a-z.

trigger: Shortest path / minimum steps in an UNWEIGHTED graph or grid
pattern: BFS with a visited set; the level at which a node is reached is its distance
notes: Use a deque. DFS does NOT give shortest paths. Weighted edges need Dijkstra instead.

trigger: Enumerate ALL combinations, permutations, subsets, or paths
pattern: DFS backtracking: choose, recurse, undo the choice
notes: Prune early when a partial choice already violates constraints. Output size is often exponential by nature.

trigger: Median or k-th element of TWO sorted arrays in log time, without merging
pattern: Binary search the partition of the SMALLER array; valid when left-max <= right-min across both
notes: Partition sizes: i + j = (m+n+1)/2. Use +/-inf sentinels for empty sides - boundary handling is where this problem is usually botched. O(log min(m, n)).

trigger: Need O(1) lookup AND O(1) ordering update at once (LRU cache, recently-used tracking, O(1) insert/delete/getRandom)
pattern: Combine two structures: hashmap for lookup + doubly linked list (or array) for order - the map stores pointers into the ordered structure
notes: LRU: map key->node, DLL with dummy head/tail; store the KEY inside the node so eviction can delete from the map. Shortcuts: Python OrderedDict.move_to_end, Java access-order LinkedHashMap.

trigger: 2D grid where water/level is bounded by the LOWEST escape path (trapping rain water II, swim in rising water)
pattern: Min-heap flood fill from the boundary: always pop the lowest wall, expand inward (Dijkstra-style)
notes: Push neighbors as max(current level, neighbor height) - a filled cell becomes a wall at the water level. The popped height is final because nothing lower is left in the heap. O(mn log(mn)).

trigger: Minimize/maximize a value where 'is x feasible?' is monotonic (capacity, speed, split sizes)
pattern: Binary search on the answer with a greedy feasibility check
notes: O(n log range). The giveaway phrase: 'smallest x such that ...' / 'largest x such that ...'.

trigger: Count ways / min cost to reach step n when each move comes from a few previous steps
pattern: 1D DP: dp[i] from dp[i-1], dp[i-2], ...; often just two rolling variables
notes: Climbing stairs, house robber, min cost climbing. Identify base cases first, then the recurrence.

trigger: Merge groups dynamically / count connected components / detect a cycle while adding edges
notes: Near O(1) amortized per operation. BFS/DFS also counts components when the graph is static.

trigger: Pairwise before/after constraints (prerequisites, build order, alphabet from sorted words) - recover an order, or just ask 'can everything finish?'
pattern: Model constraints as a directed graph, then Kahn's BFS: repeatedly take indegree-0 nodes
notes: Cycle detection is free: fewer processed nodes than the graph has = contradiction. Edge direction gotcha: [a, b] = 'b before a' means edge b->a, indegree[a]++. Unconstrained nodes start at indegree 0.

trigger: 70-minute, 4-problem assessment: how do you allocate time?
pattern: Bank Q1-Q3 first; on Q4 submit a brute force for partial credit before optimizing
notes: Target: Q1+Q2 in ~20 min. Never sit 20+ minutes on one problem with nothing submitted. Re-read the statement before coding Q3.

trigger: Long implementation-heavy statement (Q3 type): how do you avoid misreading?
pattern: List every rule/edge case as a checklist BEFORE coding; re-check the checklist before submitting
notes: Most Q3 failures are misread conditions, not algorithm gaps. Highlight numbers, ordering rules, and tie-breaking clauses.
